visual: Low, spreading alpine perennial forming a mat of narrow green leaves, topped in autumn by striking rich-blue trumpet-shaped flowers with pale striped throats.
water: Keep consistently moist during active growth; do not allow the root zone to dry out.
soil: Humus-rich, moist but sharply well-drained loam or sandy soil; acid to neutral.
soilWarning: Dislikes alkaline soil, drought and winter waterlogging; reliable drainage is particularly important.
prune: No routine pruning required; remove faded or damaged growth if needed.
hardinessNote: Hardy through most of the UK, including severe winters, provided the soil remains well drained.
resilience: Cold hardy but sensitive to drought and stagnant wet soil.
uses: Rock gardens, alpine beds, gravel gardens, containers, edging and low ground cover.

visual: Compact broadly conical tree with red flower buds opening to masses of white flowers, followed by persistent yellow-orange to orange-red crab apples.
water: Water regularly while establishing; established trees generally need additional watering only during prolonged dry periods.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sand; acid, neutral or alkaline.
prune: Pruning Group 1: little pruning is normally required; remove dead, damaged, diseased or crossing branches while dormant.
toxicity: Fruit flesh can be used when cooked, but the seeds contain potentially harmful compounds and should not be eaten.
hardinessNote: Fully hardy throughout the UK and northern Europe.
resilience: Very cold hardy and adaptable to a broad range of soils and exposures.
uses: Small gardens, wildlife gardens, specimen planting, ornamental trees and pollinator planting.

visual: Compact rounded evergreen shrub with glossy leathery foliage, producing bright-green new shoots in spring before the leaves mature to extremely dark red and burgundy tones.
water: Water regularly while establishing and keep moderately moist during dry weather, allowing excess water to drain freely.
soil: Moist but well-drained loam or sandy soil; neutral to slightly acidic.
soilWarning: Protect from severe frost, cold winds and prolonged winter wet; container plants are best moved to a sheltered position during hard freezes.
prune: Little pruning required; lightly trim in spring to maintain a compact rounded shape and remove damaged growth.
hardinessNote: Best treated as frost-tender in colder UK gardens; suitable outdoors year-round mainly in mild, sheltered locations and often safer overwintered under protection.
resilience: Generally pest- and disease-resistant but less tolerant of hard frost than many mainstream garden shrubs.
uses: Patio pots, containers, small borders, courtyard gardens and foliage displays.
uncertain: Published mature dimensions vary from approximately 0.6 m to 0.9 m.

visual: Compact multi-stemmed deciduous shrub or small tree with dark green curled foliage, fragrant white late-summer flowers, vivid red-pink persistent bracts in autumn and attractive peeling bark in winter.
water: Water regularly while establishing; once established it is relatively drought tolerant and usually needs watering only during prolonged dry spells.
soil: Moderately fertile, moist but well-drained or well-drained chalk, clay, loam or sand; acid, neutral or alkaline.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging; flowering and autumn bract colour are best in a sunny position.
prune: Little pruning is required; remove dead or badly positioned growth and lightly shape in early spring if necessary.
hardinessNote: Extremely hardy; the breeder reports frost resistance to around -25°C and the species is rated H7 by the RHS.
resilience: Very cold hardy, relatively drought tolerant once established and generally pest- and disease-free.
uses: Specimen shrub, small multi-stemmed tree, mixed borders, pollinator planting and containers.
uncertain: The breeder gives a mature height of approximately 1.5–1.8 m, while some North American material gives larger eventual dimensions.

visual: Compact upright evergreen shrub with exceptionally glossy dark brown-purple to near-black foliage edged in vivid pink, with the colours intensifying in cooler conditions.
water: Keep evenly moist while establishing, then water during prolonged dry periods; container plants require more regular watering.
soil: Free-draining loam or sandy soil or compost; acid to neutral conditions are suitable.
soilWarning: Requires free drainage and protection from hard frost; in frost-prone areas grow in a container and overwinter under protection.
prune: Little pruning is needed; lightly trim in spring to maintain shape and remove any frost-damaged growth.
hardinessNote: Half-hardy in the UK, tolerating approximately -5°C to 1°C; protect from harder frost and cold winter exposure.
resilience: Tolerates coastal conditions and some drought once established but is vulnerable to hard frost.
uses: Patio containers, summer bedding, sheltered borders, coastal gardens and foliage displays.
uncertain: Retail sources vary slightly on mature dimensions, generally placing Eclipse around 50–60 cm high and 30–45 cm wide.
